title: Beijing Lu Xun Museum

buildingCutout.basis: Only closely coincident buildings are replaced in the two separate groups, retaining the rest of the museum grounds and hutong.

terrainReference.basis: Original elevation at the preserved house’s central courtyard.

mapIdentity.provider: The named OpenStreetMap museum parcel, Overture/Tan building roofs, and independent address point for the preserved Lu Xun residence.

identities.name: Beijing Lu Xun Museum
identities.address: 19 Gongmenkou Ertiao, historic 21 Gongmenkou West Third Lane

mapIdentity.scope: OpenStreetMap way 447939893 names the museum grounds. Overture-derived building roofs set the axes and approximate positions of the historic north and south sides and the east exhibition pavilion. The former residence point was checked independently against the named map record.

note: Beijing’s cultural heritage office records a small preserved courtyard house with three bays to north and south and two per side. The museum’s own research office gives the layout and area of the rear writing room. Shizhao’s Qualla original shows the historic threshold and No. 21 plaque. EditQ’s two exact public-domain dedications show the exterior court of the permanent exhibition and its three-bay glazed pavilion.
